Where I got to
I reconstructed the tree from dump.txt — 348 of 349 files byte-identical against their recorded SHA-256 (the exception is export.sh, which contains the dump's own # FILE: banner as literal text and can't be round-tripped by any parser using that banner as a delimiter; it is excluded from the work set rather than reconstructed and guessed at).

I have not yet produced the archive. I hit the tool ceiling during survey. Here is what the survey found, because two of the three items are worth acting on before any code moves.

The §18 check: predicted 1149, observed 1151 — and I can account for both numbers exactly
claude-terminal.txt shows the suite green: total: 1151, failed: 0, succeeded: 1151, skipped: 0, twice (dotnet test and ci_local.sh --with-all --with-e2e), plus 17/17 end-to-end. Three slices of predictions finally met a run.

The arithmetic:

[Fact] + [InlineData] across the tree = 1132
SchemaMigrationRunnerTests.KeyRelations = 13 theory rows
SchemaMigrationRunnerTests.KeyColumnsAddedByAlter = 6 theory rows
1132 − 5 (its own [Fact]s already counted) + 5 + 13 + 6 = 1151. Substitute 4 for that six and you get 1149 — the predicted number, to the unit.

That is a finding, and it is F-77's shape inside the one section that exists to prevent it. §16.4 says "Four theory rows therefore name the columns that arrived by ALTER". That sentence was true of 0004. 0005 added menu_item.menu_section_identifier and menu_item_event.new_menu_section_identifier to the same TheoryData, and the sentence did not move. TestingSectionContractTests could not catch it: that gate compares assertion counts per class — 7 methods, which is still correct — and a theory-row count is not a method count. So the prediction was derived from prose the gate is structurally blind to.

Per F-77 the repair is to delete the number, not correct it — the rows are derivable from the tree, and this is the second time this exact sentence has gone stale.

A second stale count, same mechanism, one file over
Scenario 16's arithmetic comment says "Fifteen controls are expected … a rename and a reprice on the item". ManageMenuItem.razor carries four .manage-inline-form blocks, not two — Slice 38 added the position form and the comment did not move. Counting the tree: indexes contribute 5 .record-actions + 3 .page-head-action + 3 .filter-actions; details contribute 2 + 1 + 2 + 4 .manage-inline-form plus one .page-head-action on the display roster. The floor of 14 is met either way, which is why nothing reported it — a floor that passes at 15 also passes at 17.

The menu work I had scoped and was about to write
M6 Slice 43 — MoveMenuItemToSectionAsync, the last verb in the whole enhancement with no surface. Concretely:

MenuAdministration.cs — the verb, one transaction: lock the item (its LockMenuItemSql and MenuItemLockRow need menu_section_identifier), lock the target section and read MAX + 1 under it, then section_changed — plus a conditional reordered, because an item's position is within its section, so a move must append and §8.2 binds new_display_order to reordered alone. Same conditional shape CreateMenuItemAsync already uses for description_changed.
MenuWorkflow.cs — the verb, publishing MenuChanged on Moved only.
ManageMenuItem.razor — a .manage-inline-form picker (.manage-inline-form already styles select, so no CSS moves), replacing the comment that currently says the verb does not exist.
MenuAdministrationTests (26 → ~30), MenuWiringTests (18 → 19, fake gains the verb), AdministrationJourneys.MoveMenuItemToSectionAsync, and scenario 17 gains a move step at the end — moving "Apple soup" out of Starters into Puddings, where it must land after the pie, proving MAX + 1-within-target through a browser and over the §9 broadcast.
Documentation: spec → v1.28 (§7, §11.4, §16.4, Appendix A, changelog), DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md (F-90, F-91), the plan (strike the item), BUILD_PROGRESS.md whole.
Say "continue" and I'll build and deliver the archive — full files only, repo-relative, extractable at the repo root, with the Files-to-DELETE section and git add reminders. If you'd rather I split the two stale-count findings into their own slice and keep Slice 43 purely the move verb, say so and I'll cut it that way instead.

Where the slice stands
The application code and the unit/integration tests are written. I ran out of tool budget before the end-to-end harness, the documentation, and the archive. Nothing is delivered yet — no files to extract from this message.

Here is what is complete in my working tree, and the decisions inside it that are worth your veto before I finish.

Done: MoveMenuItemToSectionAsync, the last verb without a surface
src/MyRestaurant.DataAccess/Menu/MenuAdministration.cs

MoveMenuItemToSectionOutcome — four members (Moved | NoChange | MenuItemNotFound | MenuSectionNotFound), where ReorderMenuItemOutcome has three. The fourth is the whole difference: a position is a number and always exists; a heading is a row that may not.
LockMenuItemSql and MenuItemLockRow now carry menu_section_identifier — on the shared lock read rather than a query of its own, so the comparison is made against the row the transaction is holding.
UpdateMenuSectionAndPositionSql moves both columns in one statement, because a position is meaningless without the heading it is a position within.
Three rulings inside it, all flagged for veto:

A move appends to the end of the target heading. Carrying the old position across would drop the dish into the middle of somebody else's ordering at a number chosen for a different list. After this verb, "an item arriving in a heading arrives at the end of it" is one rule rather than two.
Two events, or one. §8.2 binds new_display_order to reordered alone, so a move that also changes the position writes section_changed then reordered. Conditional on the number actually differing — a move into an empty heading from position 0 lands at 0, and an event reading moved to position 0 beside an unchanged column is the noise the no-op rule exists to refuse.
Item lock first, section lock second. The only nested acquisition in the file, and consistent with every existing verb (item verbs lock an item; CreateMenuItemAsync locks a section). Two administrators moving two dishes into each other's headings therefore cannot deadlock.
MenuWorkflow.cs — the verb, publishing on Moved alone. The summary now records that no method on IMenuWorkflow is left without a surface.

ManageMenuItem.razor — a .manage-inline-form picker between Description and Position. .manage-inline-form has styled select since Slice 34, so no CSS moves. The button reads "File here", deliberately not "Move": Playwright's has-text is substring matching and the Position form's button already says "Move". Inactive headings are offered and marked, on §7's asymmetry. Pre-selected on the item's own heading, so pressing the button untouched is the reported no-op rather than a move to whichever heading sorts first.

Tests written: MenuAdministrationTests 26 → 31 (append-behind-an-existing-item, same-position-writes-one-event, already-under-that-heading, unknown section, unknown item); MenuWiringTests 18 → 19 plus the fake's new verb.

Two findings, both stale counts, both explaining a real number
F-90 accounts for your +2 exactly. §16.4 says "Four theory rows therefore name the columns that arrived by ALTER". 0005 added two more to KeyColumnsAddedByAlter and the sentence did not move. 1132 ([Fact] + [InlineData]) + 13 (KeyRelations) + 4 = 1149, the prediction; with 6 it is 1151, the run. TestingSectionContractTests is structurally blind to it — that gate compares assertion counts per class (7 methods, still correct), and a theory-row count is not a method count. Repair per F-77: delete the number.

F-91 — scenario 16's arithmetic says "a rename and a reprice on the item"; ManageMenuItem has carried four .manage-inline-form blocks since Slice 38, and my picker makes five. I am keeping the floor at 14 rather than raising it. An unobservable raise is exactly the change that turns a green suite red for no gain; the itemised census goes, the derivation rule stays, and the residual is stated.

F-92 — the spec's own opening line cites REQUIREMENTS.md (rev 5); it has been rev 6 since v1.15. The parenthetical is deleted rather than corrected, same ruling.

Remaining, and it is the second half
AdministrationJourneys.MoveMenuItemToSectionAsync (arrival barrier on the facts-grid Section link, which is the fact rather than the flash); scenario 17 gaining a final step that moves Apple soup from Starters into Puddings and reads it back behind the pie — MAX + 1-within-target proven through a browser over the §9 broadcast; spec to v1.28 (§7, §11.4, §16.4 with MenuAdministrationTests 26 → 31 and MenuWiringTests 18 → 19, Appendix A, changelog); DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md; the plan struck; BUILD_PROGRESS.md whole; _CHANGES.md; then the .tar.gz.

Say continue and I'll finish and deliver it — full files, repo-relative, extractable at the root, with the Files-to-DELETE section and git add reminders. If you want to veto the append-on-move ruling or the "File here" wording, now is the cheap moment.

Here is what is complete in my working tree, and the decisions inside it that are worth your veto before I finish.

Done: MoveMenuItemToSectionAsync, the last verb without a surface
src/MyRestaurant.DataAccess/Menu/MenuAdministration.cs

MoveMenuItemToSectionOutcome — four members (Moved | NoChange | MenuItemNotFound | MenuSectionNotFound), where ReorderMenuItemOutcome has three. The fourth is the whole difference: a position is a number and always exists; a heading is a row that may not.
LockMenuItemSql and MenuItemLockRow now carry menu_section_identifier — on the shared lock read rather than a query of its own, so the comparison is made against the row the transaction is holding.
UpdateMenuSectionAndPositionSql moves both columns in one statement, because a position is meaningless without the heading it is a position within.
Three rulings inside it, all flagged for veto:

A move appends to the end of the target heading. Carrying the old position across would drop the dish into the middle of somebody else's ordering at a number chosen for a different list. After this verb, "an item arriving in a heading arrives at the end of it" is one rule rather than two.
Two events, or one. §8.2 binds new_display_order to reordered alone, so a move that also changes the position writes section_changed then reordered. Conditional on the number actually differing — a move into an empty heading from position 0 lands at 0, and an event reading moved to position 0 beside an unchanged column is the noise the no-op rule exists to refuse.
Item lock first, section lock second. The only nested acquisition in the file, and consistent with every existing verb (item verbs lock an item; CreateMenuItemAsync locks a section). Two administrators moving two dishes into each other's headings therefore cannot deadlock.
MenuWorkflow.cs — the verb, publishing on Moved alone. The summary now records that no method on IMenuWorkflow is left without a surface.

ManageMenuItem.razor — a .manage-inline-form picker between Description and Position. .manage-inline-form has styled select since Slice 34, so no CSS moves. The button reads "File here", deliberately not "Move": Playwright's has-text is substring matching and the Position form's button already says "Move". Inactive headings are offered and marked, on §7's asymmetry. Pre-selected on the item's own heading, so pressing the button untouched is the reported no-op rather than a move to whichever heading sorts first.

Tests written: MenuAdministrationTests 26 → 31 (append-behind-an-existing-item, same-position-writes-one-event, already-under-that-heading, unknown section, unknown item); MenuWiringTests 18 → 19 plus the fake's new verb.

Two findings, both stale counts, both explaining a real number
F-90 accounts for your +2 exactly. §16.4 says "Four theory rows therefore name the columns that arrived by ALTER". 0005 added two more to KeyColumnsAddedByAlter and the sentence did not move. 1132 ([Fact] + [InlineData]) + 13 (KeyRelations) + 4 = 1149, the prediction; with 6 it is 1151, the run. TestingSectionContractTests is structurally blind to it — that gate compares assertion counts per class (7 methods, still correct), and a theory-row count is not a method count. Repair per F-77: delete the number.

F-91 — scenario 16's arithmetic says "a rename and a reprice on the item"; ManageMenuItem has carried four .manage-inline-form blocks since Slice 38, and my picker makes five. I am keeping the floor at 14 rather than raising it. An unobservable raise is exactly the change that turns a green suite red for no gain; the itemised census goes, the derivation rule stays, and the residual is stated.

F-92 — the spec's own opening line cites REQUIREMENTS.md (rev 5); it has been rev 6 since v1.15. The parenthetical is deleted rather than corrected, same ruling.

Four rulings, and how to reverse each
A move appends to the end of its new heading. Reverse by keeping item.DisplayOrder in UpdateMenuSectionAndPositionSql and dropping the conditional reordered.
Two events when the position moved, one when it didn't. §8.2 binds new_display_order to reordered alone.
MinimumControlsMeasured stays at 14. F-91's census was wrong, but the correct number is a claim about controls rendered on ten surfaces that I can't observe — an unobservable raise is the edit that turns a green suite red for nothing. Read it off a real run first.
The button says "File here", not "Move" — Playwright's has-text is substring matching and the Position form already owns "Move".
